Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 16.10.2018, the deceased Durugappa was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-36-EE-8611 on Gurugunta-Lingasugur main road and at about 11.45 am, when he was proceeding near Rafi Daba within Gurugunta Village, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Registration No.KA-36-F-1002 came from opposite side in high speed and in a rash and negligent NC: 2025:KHC-K:6637-DB HC-KAR manner and dashed against the said motorcycle.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.22,52,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. NC: 2025:KHC-K:6637-DB HC-KAR and directed the Corporation to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeals have been filed.

6. Smt. Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel appearing for the Corporation has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36-EE-8611.
The driver of the bus was examined as RW-1.

In his evidence, he has categorically stated that the deceased was proceeding in the said motorcycle at a high speed and in a rash and negligent Manappa And Anr vs Kuppanna And Anr on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185768134/
4 manner, and attempted to overtake the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36-EF-1851, which was proceeding in front of the deceased's motorcycle.

sentences.text: The deceased lost control and dashed against the motorcycle ahead of him bearing registration No.KA-36-EF-1851.
Thereafter, he lost balance and dashed the front side of the bus.
The same is evident from the IMV report marked NC: 2025:KHC-K:6637-DB HC-KAR as Ex.P6.
The Tribunal has erred in holding that the driver of the bus alone was negligent in causing the accident.
b) Secondly, the deceased, who was riding the motorcycle did not possess a driving license and had consumed alcohol, and that he was riding the motorcycle in a zigzag manner.
He tried to overtake the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36-EF-1851, lost balance and dashed against the front side of the bus.
Therefore, it is clear that the deceased also contributed to the accident.

c) Thirdly, in respect of the quantum, she has contended that even though claimants have claimed that the deceased was working as a teacher drawing a salary of Rs.20,000/- per month and was also earning an additional income of Rs.10,000/- per month as a visiting lecturer in a private college, the claimants, except producing the salary certificate marked as Ex.P24, they have not examined the author of the said document.
They have also not produced any other supporting documents.

The accident took place on a curved road.

b) Secondly, in the pleadings, RW-1 had claimed that the deceased was riding the motorcycle, attempted to overtake another motorcycle which was proceeding in front of him, dashed the Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36-EF-1851, lost balance and thereafter dashed the bus.

12. Claimant No.1/PW-1 in his deposition, has reiterated the statements made in the claim petition.
Immediately after the accident, a complaint was lodged against the driver of the bus.
As per Ex.P2-complaint, the police registered an FIR against the driver of the bus.
After thorough investigation, the Police filed a charge sheet as per Ex.P8.
So far, the driver of the bus has not challenged the charge sheet.
On the basis of the allegations of rash and negligent driving, the driver of the bus was kept under suspension by the Corporation.
This fact has been admitted by RW-1 in his cross examination.
13. In the pleadings of RW-1, it is stated that the deceased was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36-EE-8611.
In front of his motorcycle, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36-EF-1851 was proceeding in the same direction.
The deceased tried to overtake that motorcycle, lost balance and dashed the - 14 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6637-DB HC-KAR front portion of the bus.

In the evidence of RW-1, it is stated that the deceased, while riding the motorcycle, was talking on his mobile phone and did not notice the bus coming from the opposite direction, resulting in the collision.

It is very clear that there is a variance in the pleadings and the oral evidence adduced by respondent No.2.
14.
Even as per the IMV report-Ex.P6, no damage was caused to the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36- EF-1851, except that the left rear-view mirror was bent.

Considering these documents such as the FIR, complaint, charge sheet, rough sketch and IMV report, the Tribunal rightly held that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the bus and answered Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.

To prove this document, he examined PW.2- Head Master of Expert Public School,
Lingasugur.
From the documents and the evidence of PW-2, it is clear that the deceased was working as a teacher in Expert Public School, Lingasugur and drawing a salary of Rs.15,000/- per month.
In addition, it was claimed that he was also earning an income of Rs.10,000/- as a visiting lecturer in private colleges.
However, no documents have been produced to prove the same.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly held the monthly income of the deceased was Rs.15,000/- and has correctly calculated the loss of dependency.

The compensation awarded under other heads is also just and reasonable.
